page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a memory-optimized server instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 24 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is provided by a bundled 2880 GB NVMe SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top tier for single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench metrics. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, with large-block uncached read and write bandwidths ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. The server also demonstrates top-tier capabilities in software compilation, image processing, and text processing. Multi-threaded operations, database transactions, and Redis SET operations consistently register in the top 25%, while large-model LLM inference tasks perform at an average level.

From a resource density perspective, the combination of dedicated AMD EPYC processing cores, high-capacity memory, and fast local NVMe storage offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but the system is highly optimized for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, software compilation pipelines, and high-throughput web serving.
